subject: Compiler guard XXH32 on WASM128
perf_evidence: Message: 'It JITs to the same thing that slowed down SSE4 and NEON.' The guard (empty asm barrier) prevents clang from auto-vectorizing XXH32's 4-lane round loop into slow SIMD code, now also on WASM SIMD128.
change_summary: XXH32_round: the XXH_COMPILER_GUARD(acc) (empty inline asm '+r' barrier) is now also emitted when __wasm_simd128__ is defined.

units.name: asm barrier placement in XXH32_round (the perf mechanism itself)
units.evidence: inline asm barrier is the change; Alive2 cannot model inline asm (it is only modeled below as freeze/identity)

units.name: XXH32(p,len,seed) on wasm32 -msimd128, guard modeled as freeze
units.evidence: fwd+bwd correct for len 16,17,31,32,48,64,100 (72 asm->freeze rewrites on new side, 0 on old; ir differs)

notes: x86-64 IR unchanged under clang: all one-shot APIs (symbolic len) with -march=x86-64-v3 and default SSE2 give identical modules except !srcloc line metadata (x86_ident_v3/, x86_ident_sse2/). Target wasm32-unknown-unknown -msimd128; cflags -O3 -fno-strict-aliasing -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize -w -nostdlibinc -isystem _work2020/cross_sysinc -isystem c/xxHash/c9a7470/simde_inc -DXXH_NO_INLINE_HINTS=1 -mllvm -inline-threshold=100000. The SIMDe arm_neon.h stand-in is needed only because xxhash.h (since c9a7470, the parent side here) includes <arm_neon.h> on wasm simd128 when __has_include finds one, and plain clang finds its own ARM-only arm_neon.h (#error) - XXH32 does not use it; identical on both sides. Modeling: empty asm guard rewritten to freeze (xx_alive.py). Input bytes are noundef scalar args copied into a local buffer: with a raw pointer input (r_wasm_xxh32_ptr) Alive2 reports REFINES only, bwd 'Target is more poisonous than source' because freeze makes the new side defined on poison input bytes - an artifact of the freeze model, not of C semantics. Fixed lengths only (EQUIV_BOUNDED); lengths >=16 exercise XXH32_round. Commit verdict follows BRIEF lesson 7 (asm-guard-only perf change).
